items.title: Live: Trump says he 'wanted to see' as gunshots rang out and 'probably' made Secret Service act more slowly
items.description: US Acting Attorney-General Todd Blanche says the shooter apprehended at the White House correspondents' dinner was likely targeting Donald Trump. Follow live.

items.title: Teacher of the month turned assassin. Who is Cole Allen?
items.description: Details from the life of US President Donald Trump's would-be assassin paint a picture of a high achiever who took an abrupt turn towards political violence.

items.title: 'Superhero' politician shielded Kerry Kennedy at correspondents' dinner
items.description: Human rights activist Kerry Kennedy praises a "superhero" member of Congress for shielding her when an active shooter attempted to storm the annual White House Correspondents' Association dinner.

items.title: King Charles heads to US for Trump state visit after shooting incident
items.description: The British monarch and Queen Camilla are embarking on a state visit to the United States with relations between the two countries strained and following a shooting at a press gala in Washington.

items.title: Two dead in house fire on day family were due to move interstate
items.description: Two bodies found in a house that was extensively damaged by fire in the foothills of the NSW Blue Mountains are believed to be those of two unaccounted for children.

items.title: Missing 5yo girl believed to have been abducted near Alice Springs, police say
items.description: Northern Territory Police say they believe a missing five-year-old girl in Alice Springs was abducted from her home at a town camp early on Sunday morning.

items.title: Australia's fugitives found sanctuary in Istanbul. Then it all fell apart
items.description: Istanbul was once the hideout of choice for Australian crooks. Now a Sydney gangster's legal challenge has revealed how it all unravelled for the "Aussie Cartel".

items.title: Live: ASX 200 down after Wall Street rallies to record highs, oil up
items.description: The ASX 200 has lost ground, despite both the S&P 500 and tech-centric Nasdaq indexes ending last week with new record highs, while oil prices are surging with Brent crude just below $US107 a barrel. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Indigenous veteran booed at Anzac Day service 'mortified' by heckling
items.description: The Whadjuk Noongar elder who was booed while giving a Welcome to Country at Perth's Anzac Day dawn service says she had a right to speak at the event and will not back down.

items.title: Sabastian Sawe ran the marathon in an 'unbelievable time'. Here's why we can believe in it
items.description: Sabastian Sawe has smashed through one of athletics' unbreakable barriers by running a marathon faster than two hours. Some call it unbelievable, but the Kenyan runner has done everything he can to ensure it stands the test of time.

items.title: 'I know it's illegal': Artist behind 'Aussie' posters reveals new target
items.description: Peter Drew has been hanging his controversial posters around Australia for 10 years, and has no plans to stop.

items.title: 'Membership to nothing': The multi-million-dollar Wild West of rewards clubs
items.description: "Rewards clubs" have exploded in Australia, claiming to have given away hundreds of millions in prizes, but they operate with almost no legal scrutiny.

items.title: An oil shock, a federal budget and the recession we may have to have
items.description: Accompanying the oil shock unfolding in the Strait of Hormuz is a profound change in the way fiscal and monetary policymakers operate. And as the government prepares the budget with the impact of the Iran war still unfolding, a recession may be ahead.

items.title: Magnitude-6.1 earthquake and raging wildfires strike Japan's north
items.description: A preliminary magnitude-6.1 earthquake struck northern Japan early today, the US Geological Survey has reported, but there are no immediate reports of fatalities or damage.

items.title: The games developer who shuns Australian stereotypes
items.description: Developer Gregory Louden always wanted to work in games, but it was a sidestep into filmmaking that helped him secure his dream job at Finnish studio Housemarque.

items.title: 'She's like Will Ferrell': Why Kitty Flanagan said yes to Anne Edmonds
items.description: Everything Anne Edmonds has done over the last two decades has been leading to Bad Company, an unfettered satire of the theatre world the comedian created, wrote and stars in alongside Kitty Flanagan.

items.title: Why the bedroom is an 'invisible workplace' for women
items.description: There are biological and psychological reasons behind why women experience more disrupted sleep than men, but experts say the mental load is another powerful yet less obvious contributor.

items.title: Maccas wins battle to set up in 'world's coolest street'
items.description: The fast food giant has been cleared to set up an outlet in the Melbourne suburb of Northcote after successfully challenging a council decision to block its restaurant plans.

items.title: 'We live up here to escape': Residents unhappy with sand dredging proposal
items.description: A Dutch dredging company acknowledges concerns from some community members in northern Western Australia that public meetings should have been held earlier.

items.title: Law-breaking drivers to be targeted amid horror year on Queensland roads
items.description: The ABC last year revealed a sharp drop in road safety enforcement hours from police in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic.

items.title: Who's who in Tasmania's upper house elections this weekend
items.description: Voters in the Legislative Council divisions of Huon and Rosevears will head to the polls on Saturday. The outcome of the elections could determine the future of the greyhound industry in Tasmania.

items.title: Premier says algal bloom 'gone' despite expansion of fishing restrictions
items.description: Fishing restrictions will be strengthened in South Australian waters because of the algal bloom's devastating impact on stocks — but the government says the bloom itself has "essentially cleared up" along most of the state's coast.

items.title: Pogačar looks unbeatable, but Seixas could be France's next new hope
items.description: Tadej Pogačar claims a third monument win out of four for the year at Liège-Bastogne-Liège, but a new power is rising in the form of 19-year-old Paul Seixas, with an unlikely Tour de France tilt seemingly on the cards.

items.title: PNG PM says Luai's visit 'sends a message' ahead of Chiefs' NRL entry
items.description: The Wests Tigers playmaker is the Chiefs' top target ahead of their NRL entry in 2028, and the Papua New Guinea prime minister says his trip to PNG shows the interest is mutual.

items.title: Promise of $1b to fix Victorian roads in upcoming budget
items.description: The funding package also includes nearly $37 million dedicated to cleaning up graffiti along major roads.
